boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fredericktown record (October 21, 1861) in Operations to Control Missouri [June-October 1861]. The October 12-20 raid on the Iron Mountain railroad, the October 17 skirmish and the pursuit toward Greenville are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives the Union a brigade-size force of about 2,500-3,500 (the forces table records 2,500 as both bounds) and the State Guard no figure; the live field reads zero. Plummer says he marched with about 1,500 and found Carlin at Fredericktown with about 3,000, part of whom joined him; he puts Thompson's force at about 3,500 on October 26 and about 4,000 on October 31, some of their wounded saying 6,000. Thompson heard Plummer had 3,000, says the enemy came in more than double his numbers, and calls his own a victorious army of 2,000.
claims.rationale: Column sizes and mutual estimates at different dates; no return. The CWSAC range and the table's single value differ. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: Plummer found Thompson about a mile out of town on the Greenville road, with four guns masked on a hill slope about six hundred yards off and the main infantry under Lowe in a cornfield left of the road. Thompson says he placed Lowe's regiment in ambush well in front of his main line.
claims.rationale: Positions chosen by Thompson on the day; from the two opposing reports.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Brigadier General M. Jeff Thompson and Colonels J. B. Plummer and William P. Carlin. Plummer says Carlin, who claimed to rank him, reported to him for orders because Plummer had begun the battle. Plummer says Thompson commanded in person on the right; Thompson ordered the retreat by the right wing.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; no automatic sole credit to the listed commanders.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Plummer reports the total defeat and rout of Thompson's force; Thompson writes that he was victorious though he fell back before an overwhelming force. Plummer says six or seven buildings in the town were burned afterward.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads total unknown (US unknown; CS 62); the live field reads 62 (US 0; CS 62). Plummer reports 6 killed and 60 wounded, 80 prisoners taken on the field (38 wounded; 42 brought back on October 26) and 158 enemy dead buried. Thompson claims three enemy killed for every man he lost and names the loss of Colonel Lowe and his 12-pounder.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The live US zero is not a measured loss.

open_questions: Carlin's, Ross's, Marsh's, Baker's, Schofield's and the other subordinate reports, Purvis's report, returns and maps remain deferred. No nineteenth-century history covering the action was selected.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Plummer's October 26 and 31, 1861 reports and Thompson's October 20-23 dispatches are separate interested accounts from the two sides. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
